labels.caption: The saving over all-fallback of Lagged RetroRenting + one-way guard ($B_0=10\%$ of the all-fallback bill) in overflow accounting per assumption on E7's main week (120 min; medians over 1 alignment × 1 policy seed; each setting's saving over its own all-fallback cost). A bar runs from the lowest to the highest median over the row's settings (markers) and the default (grey line, -5.4%), labeled with the settings at its ends; rows sorted by span. $\Gamma$ is re-solved to keep the market tightness at its default 0.5 (in its own row, at the row's values) in every row of (b) and in the lease quantile, offered layers $V_\ell$, buffer quantile and layer GPUs rows of (c). Its allowance $B_0$ is 10\% of each run's all-fallback cost. The $\alpha_p$ and protected term rows change nothing: the policy leases no protected capacity at their settings. L-rf refuses purchases on unavailable layers, L-vr turns buffer violations into reclaims without notice (off: the default lender; on: the variant); no buffer violation occurred in its L-vr runs, so they equal the default lender's. The $\mu/\tilde{\beta}$ row reuses E7's runs. Bar ends not labeled: $\mu/\tilde{\beta}$ from 1 to 0.2; Load scenario from WAN 1 Gb/s to warm peer (Table~\ref{tab:s1-points}). Not run: the warm-peer and SSD load-rate scaling, the client unit $1/u$ and the pool width $\zeta$ (no sweep in the register); the tier map (its sweep is the default); a per-tier tokens-per-conversation factor and a clock alignment at local midnight (no source); a non-causal smoothing window and a load scenario per region pair (not built); $V_\ell$ as the whole block below the lease quantile (beyond the evaluation's memory budget); $V_\ell$ as a share of the mean lendable capacity (not defined); a uniform $\kappa$ multiplier (identical to the default).
